name: The River Delta
gloss: Silt, flood, and three harvests a year. Small, and worth more than everything around it — and the same water that feeds the harvests takes the books back a page at a time.

name: The Arable Lowland
gloss: The ordinary country most people live in, and the reason there are most people. Nothing here is remarkable, which is why every other kind is measured against it.

name: The Upland Pasture
gloss: Thin soil that carries herds rather than fields. Dry air, and a shelf of stone to build the shelves on.

name: The Deep Forest
gloss: Timber and game, and a long walk to either. Everything under the canopy is damp, including the archive.

name: The Highland Waste
gloss: Rock, weather, and the occasional stubborn holdfast. It feeds nobody and it forgets nothing: cold, dry, and no one passing through to burn what is written.
